commit_message:
Fix handling of max_fragment_length extension for PSK

A psk session was assumed to be a resumption which failed a check
when parsing the max_fragment_length extension hello from the client.

Relevant code from PR#18130 which was a suggested fix to the issue
was cherry-picked.

Fixes #18121

Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Viktor Dukhovni <viktor@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/24513)

diff --git a/include/openssl/tls1.h b/include/openssl/tls1.h
index 8ff39e3956b..8a963f62f6d 100644
--- a/include/openssl/tls1.h
+++ b/include/openssl/tls1.h
@@ -229,10 +229,12 @@ extern "C" {
 /* Allowed values for max fragment length extension */
 # define TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_512         1
 # define TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_1024        2
 # define TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_2048        3
 # define TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_4096        4
+/* OpenSSL value for unset maximum fragment length extension */
+# define TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_UNSPECIFIED 255
 
 /*
  * TLS Certificate Type (for RFC7250)
  * https://www.iana.org/assignments/tls-extensiontype-values/tls-extensiontype-values.xhtml#tls-extensiontype-values-3
  */

diff --git a/ssl/statem/extensions_srvr.c b/ssl/statem/extensions_srvr.c
index 2962a0bdcd3..699cc202c34 100644
--- a/ssl/statem/extensions_srvr.c
+++ b/ssl/statem/extensions_srvr.c
@@ -190,25 +190,30 @@ int tls_parse_ctos_maxfragmentlen(SSL_CONNECTION *s, PACKET *pkt,
                  SSL_R_SSL3_EXT_INVALID_MAX_FRAGMENT_LENGTH);
         return 0;
     }
 
     /*
-     * RFC 6066:  The negotiated length applies for the duration of the session
+     * When doing a full handshake or a renegotiation max_fragment_len_mode will
+     * be TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_UNSPECIFIED
+     *
+     * In case of a resumption max_fragment_len_mode will be one of
+     *      TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_DISABLED, TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_512,
+     *      TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_1024, TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_2048.
+     *      TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_4096
+     *
+     * RFC 6066: The negotiated length applies for the duration of the session
      * including session resumptions.
-     * We should receive the same code as in resumed session !
+     *
+     * So we only set the value in case it is unspecified.
      */
-    if (s->hit && s->session->ext.max_fragment_len_mode != value) {
-        SSLfatal(s, SSL_AD_ILLEGAL_PARAMETER,
-                 SSL_R_SSL3_EXT_INVALID_MAX_FRAGMENT_LENGTH);
-        return 0;
-    }
+    if (s->session->ext.max_fragment_len_mode == TLSEXT_max_fragment_length_UNSPECIFIED)
+        /*
+         * Store it in session, so it'll become binding for us
+         * and we'll include it in a next Server Hello.
+         */
+        s->session->ext.max_fragment_len_mode = value;
 
-    /*
-     * Store it in session, so it'll become binding for us
-     * and we'll include it in a next Server Hello.
-     */
-    s->session->ext.max_fragment_len_mode = value;
     return 1;
 }

fix_commit.message: Fix potential NULL pointer dereference in final_maxfragmentlen()
fix_commit.author: Andrey Tsygunka

findings.title: NULL pointer dereference of s->session in final_maxfragmentlen()
findings.message: final_maxfragmentlen() unconditionally dereferences s->session (via s->session->ext.max_fragment_len_mode) at the top of the function, before the existing NULL check 'if (s->session && USE_MAX_FRAGMENT_LENGTH_EXT(s->session))' further down. s->session can legitimately be NULL at this point in the handshake state machine (this extension-processing callback runs for both client and server, and in some PSK / early handshake states the session has not yet been established or resumed). This introduces a crash (NULL pointer dereference / DoS) reachable by a remote peer that drives the handshake into a state where final_maxfragmentlen() is invoked with s->session == NULL.
findings.suggestion: Move the NULL check for s->session to the very top of the function, before any dereference, and return early (success) if it is NULL, since there is nothing to do for max-fragment-length handling without a session.

ground_truth.root_cause: A new dereference of s->session was introduced above an existing NULL check for the same pointer, instead of placing the NULL check before any use of s->session. The refactor removed the old PSK-resumption-specific check (which happened to also reference s->session only after other guards) and replaced it with unconditional access, without re-validating that s->session could still be NULL at function entry in all call paths.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: NULL pointer dereference of s->session in final_maxfragmentlen()
